helpSourceNote: HELP_ARTICLES in src/lib/help-articles.ts is what /help and /help/[slug] render (src/app/(tenant)/help/page.tsx, src/app/(tenant)/help/[slug]/page.tsx). It is code, not a DB table; the markdown under docs/tutorials/ is generated recording output and is NOT the help source. Narration scripts for the same slugs live in src/lib/tutorial-scripts.ts.

articles.title: Buy a course on Learn.WitUS — browse and sign-in (signed out)
articles.notes: Lead demo A, first half. No help article corresponds. Browse-only; never fills or submits the magic-link form. Re-verified against production 2026-09-21 (witus plans/33 §1). BAM's voice; step order is frozen.

articles.title: Buy a course on Learn.WitUS — enroll (signed in)
articles.notes: Lead demo A, second half. No help article corresponds. Skips without TUTORIAL_STORAGE_STATE, and no session file exists yet (witus task 92). Default path enrolls in a FREE course (creates an enrollment row); the paid Stripe path is behind TUTORIAL_STRIPE_TEST=1 and is for test-mode previews only. Step order is frozen.

articles.title: Getting started as a teacher
articles.notes: Read-only tour of /teach: the course list, its search and status filters, the bulk bar (revealed by a client-side selection, every button asserted and none clicked), and the New course form shown but never submitted. Skips without TUTORIAL_STORAGE_STATE; the session must be an instructor, brand_admin or the platform owner.

articles.title: Create a course
articles.notes: Submitting New course writes a real course row on production. Needs either a Stripe-test/preview target or a [TUTORIAL] course the spec deletes afterwards; not attempted this session.

articles.title: Add and edit lessons
articles.notes: Adding or saving a lesson mutates published curriculum. Needs a disposable [TUTORIAL] course first (see create-a-course).

articles.title: Record lesson audio or video in the app
articles.notes: Needs microphone/camera permissions and uploads to Cloudinary, which attaches media to a real lesson. Record by hand, or against a disposable course.

articles.title: Recording scripts & teleprompter
articles.notes: Read-only: /teach/<course>/script and the full-screen teleprompter with its speed / size / mirror controls and the Recording to picker. The recorder is shown, never started (a take asks for mic/camera and an upload attaches media to a real lesson); Copy script is asserted, not clicked, because it writes the machine clipboard.

articles.title: Set a price (it's here, not in Stripe)
articles.notes: Shows Course settings -> Pricing and stops at Save settings, which is asserted and never clicked. A save step is appended ONLY under TUTORIAL_ALLOW_MUTATIONS=1 (default off, and never to be set against production): re-pricing re-prices the next checkout. Conditional at load time so marks.json matches the take.

articles.title: Organize courses with categories
articles.notes: Signed-out half only: the catalog's category chips at /courses, which is what categories are FOR. The Admin → Categories half (add/rename/delete) mutates the catalog and is not recorded.

articles.title: Publish, drafts, private, and holds
articles.notes: Every control on this article publishes or unpublishes a live course. Needs a disposable course; not attempted against production.

articles.title: Vetting a course, and the "Coming soon" page
articles.notes: Records the PUBLIC face only: a Coming-soon course page, the notify-me form and the 'Want to help this course open?' panel, both shown and never submitted (a submission creates a lead and mirrors to the WitUS Inbox). The owner's vetting queue mutates courses and is not recorded. A 7-step narrated script for the owner half already exists in src/lib/tutorial-scripts.ts.

articles.title: Add Quick-recall self-test prompts
articles.notes: Learner side needs an enrolled account and self-grading records a recall grade that feeds Recall accuracy; author side is the lesson editor. Both need a disposable course.

articles.title: Keep your course's AI features current
articles.notes: Re-index embeddings and Audit reveals both call the AI provider and bill real tokens. Show-only spec is possible later; the buttons must stay behind a default-off flag.

articles.title: Run a live session
articles.notes: Signed-out half: the public /live page. PASSES against production 2026-09-21 with no sessions scheduled, so the take shows the page and the sign-in-gated Live chat and no Live now / Upcoming / Recordings sections; the spec logs which sections were on screen. The Admin → Live half (schedule, go live, end) mutates broadcast state and is not recorded.

articles.title: Run a private class with Cohorts
articles.notes: Creating a class, inviting students by email, and adjusting a grade are all real writes about real minors. Needs a teacher session on a non-production target.

articles.title: Make someone a teacher of your school
articles.notes: Make a teacher / Remove teacher grants and revokes a real role on a real account.

articles.title: Contact a teacher or a parent (without messaging)
articles.notes: An unanswered contact request emails a real parent or teacher after 48 hours. Asserting on it would also mean reading another family's data. Needs a seeded non-production school.

articles.title: Give parents a read-only Family view
articles.notes: /family shows one real child's grades and attendance. Never record it against production data; needs a seeded demo family.

articles.title: Notes, highlights, and class notes
articles.notes: Writing a note, sharing it, or sending a class note all persist. Needs an enrolled tutorial learner and a cleanup step.

articles.title: Search inside a course
articles.notes: Read-only. The Search this course box renders only for an enrolled learner, an editor or an invited auditor, so the session must be enrolled in (or own) TUTORIAL_COURSE_PATH. The article omits the auditor case that the code allows.

articles.title: See learner feedback and problem reports
articles.notes: Signed-out half: the site-wide 🐞 Report a problem popover, opened and typed into but NEVER submitted (a submission files a real report and mirrors to the WitUS Inbox). The teacher-side queues (/teach → Curriculum feedback, Admin → Problem reports) show other people's reports and are not recorded.

articles.title: Sharing, previews, and cross-promotion
articles.notes: Signed-out: the Share popover on a course page. Copy link is NOT clicked — each channel click POSTs a share count to /api/share, which would inflate the admin dashboard's share signals.

articles.title: When your lesson names another course
articles.notes: The learner-facing Related courses list only renders where the owner has already approved a candidate; the /admin/cross-links queue mutates on approve. Needs a seeded target.

articles.title: Marketing: promo codes, announcements, and demand
articles.notes: A 7-step narrated script already exists in src/lib/tutorial-scripts.ts. Promo-code creation mirrors to a real Stripe coupon and announcement batches push drafts to the WitUS Outbox, so every write on the page needs a default-off flag.

articles.title: Sales and promotions (no promo code needed)
articles.notes: Signed-out half: the public /sale index — what is running now, starting soon, and ended. The Admin half starts and ends real sales and is not recorded. PASSES against production 2026-09-21, but it filmed the EMPTY STATE: no promotion on learn.witus.online carries a slug today, so the clip is only worth keeping once a campaign is live. The spec logs which face it filmed.

articles.title: Streaming: always-on stream + multistream to socials
articles.notes: Saving an always-on embed or a multistream target stores live broadcast config, and stream keys are secrets that must never appear in a recording.

articles.title: Quizzes: rotating pools, shuffled options, and images
articles.waiver: Quizzes are authored in quiz_content through seed files (scripts/data/, scripts/seed-*.ts), not in any screen: questionsPerAttempt, shuffleOptions and imageUrl/imageAlt are data fields a developer edits in a repo and re-seeds. There is no UI to click, so there is nothing to record.

articles.title: Lesson images (with alt text) and Quick recall
articles.notes: The lesson editor's Image button uploads to Cloudinary and edits published lesson text. Needs a disposable course.

articles.title: Recording long lessons (auto-split parts)
articles.notes: The behaviour this article describes only appears after a take passes the ~100 MB upload cap. Not a waiver — there IS a screen — but it cannot be produced in a short scripted run; record it by hand off a real long take.

articles.title: Keeping courses & content current (migrate + seed)
articles.waiver: This article is a command-line runbook: pnpm db:migrate:prod, then the seed that owns the course (seed:courses, seed:languages, seed:faa …). Its only screen is a terminal, and the one in-app sentence it carries (edit lesson text on the Curriculum tab) is covered by add-and-edit-lessons. Nothing to record in the browser.

articles.title: Change a course's instructor (fix wrong bylines)
articles.notes: Changing the Instructor dropdown moves a live course to another account and CHANGES ITS PUBLIC URL, breaking every existing link. Never against production.

articles.title: Embed your courses in another app (API keys)
articles.notes: Signed-out half: the two public paste-anywhere embeds, /embed/card/<id> and /embed/course/<id>. The key half is deliberately NOT recorded — /admin/api-keys shows a full API key exactly once, and a recording of that screen is a leaked credential.

articles.title: Your admin home and brand settings
articles.notes: Read-only walk of /admin and /admin/settings. No toggle is flipped and Save changes is never clicked: these settings change the live school for every visitor. The tiles hold real counts, so the captions describe the rule and never read out a number.
